# Cities of Naggaroth

*Page PDF 12*

## **Cities of Naggaroth**
Six great cities are home to almost the entire Druchii population. Behind their bleak walls, black towers thrust into stormy skies, each is the mansion of a dreadlord, nobles who both serve and scheme against the drachau and, through them, Malerion. Suspended bridges and platforms allow the dreadlords and their servants passage between the towers without venturing into the warren of streets below, whilst high-walled houses keep the narrow, winding alleys in perpetual shadow. Each dwelling is fortified, as no dark elf trusts their fellow citizens. 

## **Naggarond**
Central to Naggaroth is Naggarond, first city and Malerion’s seat between the foothills of the Iron Mountains and the Sea of Malice. It is said a hundred towers rise behind its walls, but none rise higher than Malerion’s. Most are home to the highborn nobility, though some sit abandoned, their residents slaughtered and forgotten. These forsaken towers are not empty, for flocks of harpies, tormented spectres, and worse dangers are said to haunt their halls. 

## **Five Deadly Poisons**
vaeric of the Bleeding Moon is an assassin from har ganeth, determined to become an expert killer with five rare venoms found around the world. in 2511 iC, vaeric crept aboard _Temple of Spite_ and set about acquiring each one. he has gathered aquatic Lustrian centipede venom, the secretions of graheim’s beaded toad, and naga venom from the marshes of Khuresh. Vaeric needs help in finding crater lizard poison from the Dark Lands and tomb scorpion venom from Nehekhara, through trade, theft, or subterfuge. 

## **Hag Graef**
Hag Graef, meaning Dark Crag, is a city of eternal shadow, squatting at the bottom of a deep chasm. Only the topmost floors of its eight towers know any natural light, while below them the maze of streets and alleys are lit only by torch, lamp, and witchlight. The mines are rich in precious metals and warpstone, and so its dreadlords field impressive armies, at the core of many expeditions from Naggaroth. There is no shortage of Druchii to serve in them, for life is so bleak at the bottom of the canyon that many of Hag Graef ’s citizens become soldiers or corsairs just to escape. 

## **Ghrond**
While its mines are a source of fabulous wealth, the city and tower of Ghrond are most notable as the home of the only dark elf approaching Malerion’s power: his mother, the seeress Morathi. From atop the Tower of Prophecy, Morathi and the sorceresses of the Dark Convent read the skies over the evershifting Chaos Wastes and send their predictions and warnings directly to Malerion. 

## **Karond Kar**
Standing cold and bleak along the shores of the Sea of Chill, Karond Kar is where the great fleets of Druchii reavers dock to sell their living cargoes. Most captives are sold in open auction to agents of the various dreadlords, their torments providing entertainment to the lowborn crowds. Asur and other elf captives are highly prized and are sold at private auction in the mansions of the merchants. 

## **Har Ganeth**
Alone among the cities of the Druchii, murder and theft are illegal in Har Ganeth for most of the year, the punishment for any violation being death by sacrifice atop Khaine’s great temple. This is the law of the ruler, Crone Hellebron, because the influence of Khaine is so great that residents would otherwise gleefully murder each other until none were left. These passions are unleashed on Death Night, when the whole population is unfettered to indulge in wanton slaughter. 

## **Clar Karond**
Clar Karond is Naggaroth’s shipyard, building the black vessels that harrow the world. The city sits across the Redvenom River, in a broad valley bounded by the Nightsreach Mountains, where it meets the Sea of Malice. The shipyards and city docks are found on the eastern bank of the river, whilst the tall manors and private docks of the city stand to the west. Clar Karond is also home to Naggaroth’s greatest beastmasters, those servants of Anaeth Raema who raise cold ones for Malerion’s knights and goad great monsters into his warhosts and fleets. 

## **Har Kaldra**
Left unspoken, save in whispers, is Har Kaldra, the Forgotten City. Its rulers once conspired against Malerion and, in a night of unspeakable magic and horror, paid the price. Now empty, devoid of all life and even the souls of the damned, it stands as a reminder of what happens when one defies the Dread King. 

## **The Watchtowers**
to defend themselves from the hordes of Chaos that roam the frozen wastelands to the north, the Druchii have founded many great citadels. Each of these watchtowers is the size of a city, provisioned to withstand years of siege and garrisoned with a great host of dark elf warriors. thus, threats from the realm of Chaos have been held at bay, for now.
